changelog: fix: the backend could silently run a job against a different taxonomy database than the one the user chose and the Job Detail panel displayed. Database resolution lived inside the worker, AFTER run_params.json had been written, and whenever it judged the user's choice unusable it quietly swapped in something else — or, finding nothing, passed an empty --dbPath to R, whose own fallback then picked 'the first available file' in databases/ (on one machine an EMU species_taxid.fasta). Resolution now happens in /run before anything is recorded: an explicit choice is either used or the job is REFUSED with an explanation, automatic resolution happens only when nothing was selected and is recorded as such, and run_params.json carries dbPath_requested, dbPath_resolved and dbPath_auto so the panel can no longer disagree with the run. A *_toSpecies_trainset is no longer rejected for its name. R's fallback searches recursively, accepts only trainset-shaped files, and stops rather than guessing. The upload screen shows the server's reason instead of 'Failed to start analysis.'. Also: assignTaxonomy() is now seeded — the same reads against the same database moved 39 ASVs at genus level between two runs because the bootstrap RNG was unseeded.
